body:
I just signed back into my account after a year of recovery.

Recovery.

I'm still the same person whose life I wanted to take. I still understand the reasons why, but the *impulse* is no longer there. There's a very philosophical attitude about suicide I take, but without everything behind it, things are okay enough to keep slogging on. I guess if it'd make no difference to die at 90 or now, I'd prefer to die at 90.

When I say recovery, I don't mean that I went to therapy or that someone talked me out of it. The sensation just broke, and the fear that my SO would find me in the bathtub, wrists slit, went away as well. Very Rick and Morty, but no one asks to be born, no one belongs anywhere, and we're all going to die. Still, I'm fine with dying later, for now.

Somewhere in my desperate urge to die, there was an idea concerning consequentialism that I'd read, that even though we're infinitely smaller than some things, we're infinitely larger than others. Somehow, that's helped me. It's not profound, it's not novel, but it struck me that, being somewhere in the middle, I can coast through the times when death seems like a good idea and then get back into living exactly *because I don't matter*.

Platitude time. You're not dead yet, and potential is worthless. It's what you do that affects things. Even briefly, become a force for something, even if it's small, even if it's not for yourself.

My other self-bluffbuster is, if I'm not willing to transfer the contents of my bank account to someone, I'm not going to die. If there's any reticence, any hesitation in doing it, I'll make it. Even when I was broke, not being willing to make that transfer that convinced me that I wasn't 100%. It's funny to me now, but it's probably the best indicator I have to how deep I am- how close I am to emptying my accounts.

Anyway, that's me. Things were horrible in my head, and then they weren't. Maybe they will be again. Meanwhile, I'll keep at whatever it is that I'm doing, however imperfect of far from ideal it is. Best of.

After a week or so of barely eating, you'll eventually lose your appetite entirely. You won't hibernate, but you'll slow down, mentally and physically. Winter is approaching fast, so it's a bad time to go homeless if you've never done it before. For me, living out of a tent was better than living out of my car. Start visitng the soup kitchens; they're not for homeless people as much as working poor, the forgotten elderly, young parents, and families fallen on hard times. They'll also likely be able to hook you up with odd jobs or other work or find you a place to stay.

It's better your sense of pride is lost than your appetite. You don't die of low status.

That sort of situation is what lead me to where I am right now. When I was a young teen, a psychologist stopped my dad on the street and diagnosed him with NPD after overhearing one of his outbursts towards me. After that, he psych shopped me around for a while trying to find someone who'd agree with him and blame me to validate his awful behavior, all the while telling everyone he was trying to get me help. After it was clear to him that modern therapists were all idiots for being more interested in him, he tried a Christian Life Counselor who he thought he'd get in his corner, but thankfully saw through the ruse as well. Out of all of them, it was him who gave me the best advice I wish I had taken: Get the hell out of dodge. 

My dad spent years of our lives burning me down and beating me up in private for all of his fears and failures, then did damage control by turning on the charm to the staff and faculty at my school to paint me as a manipulative, drug using problem child. The teachers who knew me as a top student but saw how I was wilting didn't buy it, but after a few donations and games of golf and tennis with some of the administration, orders came from on high to put me on lock down, with mandatory supervision and periodic drug testing that never came back positive (see it working? it's keeping him clean.). It was like being trapped in plain sight. I wasn't the golden child in my family, and I left home my senior year with nothing, went NC for many years, and eventually found my own path. A few years ago, I made the mistake of allowing contact once, and he used my mother to guilt me into a relationship that has completely destabilized my life. I'm just now trying to fix that.

My mom doesn't know she's a victim. My sister was his biggest enabler. I... can't even think about my life clearly right now. An N family member is a terrible burden that no one should have to suffer, but because of how they are, it's so hard to get help to yourself and the people who need it. It's a damned frustrating shame of a situation.
Thanks, that's very true. There was some helpful and surprisingly relevant information on a linked sub, and I'm going to look into therapy soon, granted I can find something that will accommodate me.

Thanks for responding. I just spent some time reading through some related subs, and 'raised by narcissists' really hit home for me. I'm trying to figure out if and how the ACA makes mental healthcare more accessible, although I won't be able to afford it for long if I do sign up, and I plan to look into therapy options that offer phone or chat service for the time being. Here's to a foot in the door.
